data.name: Devanayagi
data.gender_notes: Devanayagi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Devi (Goddess) + Nayagi (Lady or Goddess of). This name signifies the goddess who rules over all other gods. The name Devanayagi carries the meaning “Goddess of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devanayagi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents divine feminine power and grace.
data.etymology: Devanayagi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devanayagi total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Devanayagi" is prominent in Tamil Nadu, India and holds a significant cultural importance in the Hindu religion. It is believed that Goddess Devanayagi, also known as Devi, Mariamman, or Amman, holds the power to protect her devotees from childhood ailments, health issues, and a variety of other problems. In some regions, she is also worshipped for fertility, prosperity, and as a goddess of love and relationships. The name "Devanayagi" highlights the immense power and divinity of the goddess that rules over other gods.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Devanayagi" lies in its association with the divine feminine, the Mother Goddess who is believed to be the embodiment of compassion, love, and nurturing. She is the giver of life, the healer of illnesses, and the suppressor of negative emotions. The name "Devanayagi" is a reminder of the omnipotent and benevolent power of the divine goddess and her ability to provide protection, peace, and happiness to her devotees. It is a call to seek her blessings, guidance, and strength in times of need.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Devanayagi: Goddess who grants the blessings of the gods. She is the divine intercessor, bridging the gap between the divine and the human realm.

historical_references.reference: Devanayagi, also known as Devanambi, was a queen who ruled the Chola kingdom during the late 11th and early 12th centuries. She is best known for her patronage of the temple town of Thanjavur, where she built the beautiful Brihadesvara Temple.

Another reference to Devanayagi comes from the Tamil epic, Cilappatikaram. In this work, she is mentioned as the wife of Agastya Muni, a renowned sage. This reference indicates her importance in Hindu mythology and religious beliefs.
